title: Thrombus characterization using MRI in intermediate-high-risk patients with pulmonary embolism and catheter-based interventional treatment
summary:
Pulmonary embolism can manifest itself as limited physical activity, dizziness, chest pain, coughing up blood or shortness of breath. The disease can be potentially fatal. In these severe cases, it is possible to treat the pulmonary artery embolism with special catheters in addition to blood thinning. It is possible remove the blood clots from the pulmonary arteries using catheters. Another treatment method can dissolve the blood clot in the lungs. For this purpose, medication is administered locally via a special catheter. Both procedures help to quickly relieve heartn strain. To further improve catheter-based treatment options for severe pulmonary embolism, more knowledge about the composition of blood clots is needed.
With the help of a magnetic resonance imaging and laboratory tests of blood clots, a distinction can be made between an acute and less acute pulmonary artery embolism.  An MRI scan will be carried out on patients with pulmonary artery embolism and the blood clot will be removed from the pulmonary vessels using a catheter followed by histopathological examination. The composition and age of the blood clots, determined by MRI scan, could predict the effectiveness of a possible catheter-based treatment and could help to determine the safest and most effective procedure for the patient.
conditions: Pulmonary embolism with mention of acute cor pulmonale
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1.) Age from 18 years up to and including 85 years
2.) Confirmed acute pulmonary artery embolism using CTPA (computed tomographic pulmonary angiography)
3.) Diameter ratio between right and left ventricles (RV/LV) ≥ 1 in CT scan or echocardiography
4.) Concentration of troponin T above the detection limit
5.) PESI Score III-V
Exclusion criteria:
1.) Hemodynamic instability
2.) Pregnancy or breastfeeding
3.) Low-risk pulmonary artery embolism
4.) Earlier inclusion in the study
